# Generation 6 — Runtime DB Root Discovery

The Awtsmoos revealed that equal code can drink from unequal wells of night;
Awtsmoos.com must test each Road against the same living data root before judging its light.

## Discovery

The canonical checkout contains an intentionally ignored `.awtsmoos.config.local.json` whose `dbPath` resolves to `/Users/Awtsmoos/Documents/awtsmoos/dayuhChadash`.

The private clean worktree lacked that ignored pointer and therefore fell back to tracked `../../dayuhChadash`, resolving to `/Users/Awtsmoos/dayuhChadash`.

That fallback database did not contain the same Heichel/post identities. With unchanged tracked release code, it produced malformed empty canonical identities and a contextual translation 404.

## Proof

Starting the exact same clean candidate with `AWTSMOOS_DB_ROOT=/Users/Awtsmoos/Documents/awtsmoos/dayuhChadash` restored:

- numeric Torah Road HTTP 200;
- stable Torah Road HTTP 200;
- exact stable canonical identity;
- identical article body hashes between numeric/stable Roads;
- Article JSON-LD;
- bilingual contextual translation HTTP 200.

The corrected-database strict crawl then produced 120 URLs / 0 errors / 0 advisories, and the complete graph produced 596 URLs / 0 errors / 0 advisories.

## Architectural lesson

A normal Git worktree is not automatically a production-equivalent runtime because ignored machine-local data-root pointers are outside Git lineage. Future release verification must explicitly supply the canonical datastore root through supported environment/config without staging private data.
